guide.title: What the platform does not keep
guide.subtitle: No message bodies, and why two fields still matter
guide.excerpt: Message content is not archived. What is kept is metadata — and among that metadata two fields are load-bearing, because without them a bill could not be reconciled.

p: The platform does not persist message bodies. A send is a pass-through: the text goes to the provider, and what comes back is recorded. This is a compliance position rather than a storage saving — holding message content creates obligations the service is not designed to carry.
The direct consequence is that the platform cannot re-derive anything from the text later. Keep your own record on the business side.

sections.h: Two fields you should actually read
p: Because the body is gone, the encoding that was used and the number of billable segments cannot be recomputed after the fact. Both are returned on the send response and kept on the record — which makes them the ground truth for reconciliation.

The split between how many requests were submitted and how many segments were billed is also deliberate. One long message is a single request and several billable segments, so a month where request count and billed count differ is normal, not a discrepancy.

sections.scope: Retention and the metadata-only log apply to every channel — the same window covers all three.
